shinyOAuth

shinyOAuth is an R package for OpenID Connect (OIDC) authentication and OAuth 2.0 authorization in Shiny apps. Users can sign in with existing accounts and give your app permission to call APIs on their behalf.

The package works across OAuth 2.0 and OIDC providers, including services such as Google, Microsoft, Auth0 and Okta, and self-hosted providers such as Keycloak. You can use built-in provider helpers, discover OIDC settings automatically, or connect to other providers by configuring their endpoints and authentication settings yourself.

The Shiny module manages the sign-in process, from redirects and callbacks to OIDC token validation, user information and token refresh. Your Shiny app can use authentication status, tokens and user information as reactive values. You can also reuse the user’s sign-in with other R packages and database drivers that accept OAuth access tokens. shinyOAuth supplies a current token, refreshing it when needed.

Features

  • Shiny module: oauth_module_server() manages login, callbacks and token refresh. It returns reactive values for login status, tokens and user information.

  • S7 classes: OAuthProvider, OAuthClient and OAuthToken describe the provider, your app’s registration and the tokens it receives.

  • Functions for custom integrations: use prepare_call(), handle_callback(), introspect_token() and refresh_token() to manage the flow yourself.

  • Provider setup: use built-in helpers for GitHub, Google, Microsoft, Keycloak and Auth0, discover OIDC settings with oauth_provider_oidc_discover(), or configure a provider yourself.

  • Security: AES-GCM-encrypted state, single-use server-side state, origin- and tab-scoped browser binding, HTTPS enforcement and PKCE (S256). OIDC checks cover ID token signatures and claims, including nonce, and match the UserInfo subject to the ID token. DPoP, mTLS, JAR and PAR are available for providers that require them. See vignette("authentication-flow", package = "shinyOAuth") (online guide).

  • Asynchronous execution: provider requests can run in background workers to keep other Shiny sessions responsive. See the setup instructions.

  • Diagnostics: record login successes, failures and other events with audit hooks or OpenTelemetry. See vignette("audit-logging", package = "shinyOAuth") (online guide) and vignette("opentelemetry", package = "shinyOAuth") (online guide).

Installation

Install from CRAN:

install.packages("shinyOAuth")

Install the development version from GitHub:

if (!requireNamespace("remotes", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("remotes")
}

remotes::install_github("lukakoning/shinyOAuth")

Usage

See vignette("usage", package = "shinyOAuth") (online guide) for login buttons, authenticated API calls, configuration and a deployment checklist.

Minimal example

Register a GitHub OAuth app in your GitHub Developer Settings, using http://127.0.0.1:8100 as the callback URL. Set GITHUB_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID and GITHUB_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET in your R environment before running the example. The environment setup instructions show how to store these values in .Renviron.

library(shiny)
library(shinyOAuth)

# GitHub OAuth 2.0 provider has been preconfigured in the package
#  - You can quickly configure OIDC providers with `oauth_provider_oidc_discover()`
#  - You can manually configure every other provider with `oauth_provider()`
provider <- oauth_provider_github()

# Build client using your app's ID, secret, & redirect URI:
client <- oauth_client(
  provider = provider,
  client_id = Sys.getenv("GITHUB_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID"),
  client_secret = Sys.getenv("GITHUB_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET"),
  redirect_uri = "http://127.0.0.1:8100",
  scopes = c("read:user", "user:email")
)

# Simple UI
ui <- oauth_ui(fluidPage(
  # Show login information:
  uiOutput("login_information")
), id = "auth", client = client)

# Server which obtains authentication
server <- function(input, output, session) {
  # Start authentication module; will automatically redirect unauthenticated users
  #   to the provider's login page and handle the callback
  # Returns reactive values with authentication status, token details, user info,
  #   etc.
  auth <- oauth_module_server("auth", client)

  # Render login information:
  output[["login_information"]] <- renderUI({
    if (auth[["authenticated"]]) {
      user_info <- auth[["token"]]@userinfo
      tagList(
        tags[["p"]]("You are logged in! Your details:"),
        tags[["pre"]](paste(capture.output(str(user_info)), collapse = "\n"))
      )
    } else {
      tags[["p"]]("You are not logged in.")
    }
  })
}

runApp(
  shinyApp(ui, server), port = 8100,
  launch.browser = FALSE
)

# Open the app in your regular browser at http://127.0.0.1:8100
# (viewers in RStudio/Positron/etc. cannot perform necessary redirects)

On Posit Connect or Connect Cloud, open the direct app URL in a new browser tab or window to test login. The dashboard’s embedded preview can prevent OAuth redirects. On Connect Cloud, copy the sharing URL from Settings > URL. Register the exact public callback URL with your provider. See deployment instructions.

Logging/auditing

Use audit hooks to record callbacks and login outcomes, or send logs and traces to a monitoring service through OpenTelemetry.

For R hook examples, see vignette("audit-logging", package = "shinyOAuth") (online guide). For exporter setup, see vignette("opentelemetry", package = "shinyOAuth") (online guide).

More information

Authentication flow explains login requests, callbacks and token checks. Before deployment, work through the security checklist. You can also read these guides in R with vignette("authentication-flow", package = "shinyOAuth") and vignette("usage", package = "shinyOAuth").

For developers: tests & integration tests

The ‘testthat’ tests are in tests/testthat/. Integration tests in integration/keycloak/ use a local Keycloak instance in Docker or Podman and include browser tests with ‘shinytest2’ and ‘chromote’. Demo deployments are in integration/gcp/ for Google Cloud Run and integration/posit/ for Posit Connect Cloud.
